title: Corp MDM Spyware Targets Logistics Firms, Steals New SMS and Redirects Calls
description: The logistics sector has become the target of a new malicious cyber campaign that distributes an Android spyware codenamed Corp MDM. Uses fake Google Play pages branded as CEVA and TKW Logistics to distribute an Android Package Kit (APK) file disguised as an MDM system service.
content:
The logistics sector has become the target of a new malicious cyber campaign that distributes an Android spyware codenamed Corp MDM.

According to Have I Been Squatted, the campaign uses fake Google Play pages branded as CEVA and TKW Logistics to distribute an Android Package Kit (APK) file that's dressed up as a system service. The delivered app has the package name 'com.corp.mdm'. Once installed, the malware requests broad permissions allowing it to read SMS messages, forward two-factor authentication tokens, and reroute sensitive operational calls.
author: The Hacker News

title: Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators
description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and CISA publish joint guidance urging critical infrastructure operators to enforce principle of least privilege (PoLP) and strict supply chain verification for third-party industrial control systems (ICS) and SCADA vendors.
content:
The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) have released joint guidance to highlight considerations for critical infrastructure entities to reduce risk and minimize vulnerabilities when working with third-party industrial control system (ICS) integrators.

Critical infrastructure owners and operators should maintain caution when granting third-party ICS integrators high levels of access or control over industrial processes, ensuring the principle of least privilege (PoLP) is applied.
author: CISA / FBI

title: One URL, Three Different Tricks: Anatomy of an Evasive Phishing Vector
description: SANS ISC handlers analyze a crafted phishing payload that exploits three distinct protocol normalization anomalies to bypass perimeter secure email gateways (SEGs) and endpoint web inspection engines.
content: SANS Internet Storm Center handlers received a phishing email containing an intricate multi-stage payload. At first sight, it looks like garbage, but every piece of it has been carefully crafted to confuse basic security controls and security gateways.
author: Xavier Mertens (SANS ISC)

title: TeamFiltration Campaign Compromises Seven Microsoft 365 Accounts Using Default Passwords
description: Cybersecurity researchers disclose details of an active TeamFiltration campaign codenamed UNK_CondorFiltration targeting over 5,700 accounts across 28 Microsoft 365 tenants from 1,487 unique AWS EC2 source IPs.
content:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of an active TeamFiltration campaign codenamed UNK_CondorFiltration that has targeted over 5,700 accounts across 28 Microsoft 365 tenants.

According to Proofpoint, the activity has primarily focused on Chilean retail and financial institutions. It originated from 1,487 unique AWS EC2 source IP addresses.
author: The Hacker News

title: Attackers Exploit WordPress CVE-2026-87902 Within Hours of Public Disclosure
description: Threat actors have begun actively exploiting a critical 9.2 CVSS vulnerability in WordPress (CVE-2026-87902) that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to trigger arbitrary local PHP file inclusion and RCE.
content:
Threat actors have begun to actively exploit a critical security flaw in WordPress within hours of public disclosure.

The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-87902 (CVSS score: 9.2), which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to obtain remote code execution (RCE).
author: The Hacker News

title: Data Broker Radaris Loses Key Domains in Privacy and Wiretapping Legal Battle
description: A federal judge grants an emergency injunction seizing core domain assets of people-search data broker Radaris following class action filings detailing illicit scraper infrastructure and privacy violations.
content: Data broker Radaris has lost control of several prominent Internet domain names after a federal judge granted an emergency injunction requested by plaintiffs in a class-action lawsuit accusing the company of violating state and federal privacy and wiretapping statutes.
author: Brian Krebs

title: Attackers Use Malicious Terraform Providers to Deliver Go Malware via HashiCorp Registry
description: Researchers uncover poisoned Terraform providers and Go modules hosted on the public HashiCorp Registry designed to execute post-installation payloads on developer infrastructure during terraform init.
content: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed Go-based malware distributed via two Go Modules and two Terraform providers, marking the first time threat actors are using the centralized repository hosted by HashiCorp as a distribution vector for malicious payloads.
author: The Hacker News

title: MikroTrick Chain Let Attackers Take Over MikroTik Routers Without Password or SSH Key
description: Two chained MikroTik RouterOS vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-67279 & CVE-2026-86060) allow unauthenticated remote attackers on the Internet to achieve root shell execution without credentials.
content:
Two MikroTik RouterOS SSH vulnerabilities chained together let attackers take full administrative control of Internet-exposed routers without a password, SSH key, or completed authentication.

The chain, which CERT Polska calls MikroTrick, combines an SSH state-machine flaw (CVE-2026-67279) with an argument-injection bug in the RouterOS login process (CVE-2026-86060).
author: The Hacker News

title: New Windows Malware ClosedQuorum Built to Let Four AI Models Vote on Its Next Move
description: Cisco Talos uncovers a novel malware architecture named CLOSEDQUORUM designed to query four disparate AI LLM endpoints in parallel to reach consensus on reconnaissance commands, evasions, and token exfiltration.
content:
A Windows malware called CLOSEDQUORUM is built to take orders from a vote of up to four AI models instead of an attacker's server, Cisco Talos said on September 22.

The models can choose to steal Windows credentials, saved browser passwords, and crypto wallet data based on situational context gathered from the target host.
author: Cisco Talos / THN
